Alice / Dan — thanks again. Attached is a short reference bundle: a one-page architecture diagram and a connectivity checklist. High-level answers below; we'll walk these on the call and can provide more granular configuration snippets as needed.

Summary (short):
- Control plane: Redwood operates a managed control plane (redwood-control.redwood.ai) that requires outbound TLS (HTTPS) from the customer VPC to the control-plane endpoints. For enterprise/private deployments we offer a Private Control Plane option that uses a VPC endpoint or a customer-hosted control-plane proxy. No inbound firewall openings are required for our default hosted control plane.
- Data plane: The serving/data plane is deployed inside customer-owned subnets (Private VPC) when you choose Redwood Private. Models run on instances with private ENIs and attach to customer-managed storage if requested. Customer data remains inside the VPC; we only send tokenized telemetry and health pings to the telemetry endpoint if you opt in.

Networking checklist (excerpt):
- Required outbound (egress) to: control-plane (https://control.redwood.ai) and telemetry (https://telemetry.redwood.ai). We can provide CIDR ranges for firewall allowlists — see attached checklist.
- DNS: control.redwood.ai and telemetry.redwood.ai must resolve to public IPs unless Private Control Plane is used (then a private endpoint will be provided).
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS) outbound for control/telemetry; 22 only if you request a bastion for ops (optional).
- VPC design: recommended isolate data-plane subnets (no public IPs), separate mgmt subnets for bastion/admin. Use NAT Gateway for controlled outbound egress.
- Peering/Transit: We support VPC Peering and Transit Gateway designs. For multi-account setups, recommend Transit Gateway and centralized NAT to simplify egress allowlists.

Security/keys & audit:
- KMS/HSM: Support for customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) and bring-your-own-HSM via PKCS11 connectors for the Private on-prem package. Data-plane disk encryption uses customer keys if configured.
- Audit logs: Control-plane actions, model deploy events, and admin access logs can be streamed to your S3/GCS bucket or pushed to a SIEM via secure delivery. Retention/filters are configurable.

Alice — quick written answers below so your reviewers have something to reference ahead of Wed's call. Rafael and Monica will expand on these during the walkthrough.

1) Control plane allowlist / TLS
- We provide a stable set of egress IP ranges for control-plane and telemetry endpoints; these are published in our enterprise allowlist doc and also pushed to customers' hub records (see Drive link). We'll send the CIDRs as a short CSV prior to the call.
- Server-side TLS is sufficient for the default hosted control plane. For customers requiring mutual authentication, we support mTLS via our Private Control Plane option (requires certificate exchange and short-lived client certs).

2) Data-plane isolation & telemetry
- Data-plane: For Redwood Private on VPC, inference payloads and model artifacts are stored and processed inside customer-managed subnets — no model payloads are sent to Redwood public data endpoints.
- Telemetry: Minimal telemetry consists of anonymized health metrics and instance heartbeats (instance id, uptime, metrics counters). Telemetry is opt-in; for air-gapped/on-prem installs telemetry is disabled by default.

3) KMS/HSM integration
- We support AWS KMS & GCP CMEK for cloud-based installs. For on-prem/air-gapped installs we can integrate with customer HSMs via PKCS11 (we have a tested connector used in two customer deployments). Rafael will bring the connector docs and sample config on the call.

4) NAT/egress guidance
- Recommend reserved /20 per AZ for serving subnets to allow for scaling and health replacement (adjust by expected replica counts).
- Expect conservative 100 concurrent outbound TLS connections per 1000 QPS as a baseline — we will run a small performance estimate for Acme once we have QPS/latency targets.
